rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Evidence: the course needs an average of about 1.5 m/s to finish in 3 s, and base_speed of 2 gives full PWM, so I set base_speed to 1.6 for speed headroom while keeping some margin for the controller. Geometry: five sensors spaced 15 mm apart across x = -0.03 to +0.03 m (wider than the 25 mm tape, so at least one sensor sees the line at all times) and placed 50 mm ahead of the axle so the controller reacts before the wheels reach a bend. Sensor size is 12 mm, a compromise between resolution and coverage. Weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 make the signal proportional to lateral offset (positive = left, which steers left). Gains: kp = 2.0 gives a moderate correction (about 1.0 signal -> 700 PWM difference); kd = 0.1 damps the oscillation a proportional-only loop would produce at this speed; ki = 0.05 is small to avoid integral windup on curves. line_loss is last_direction so the robot recovers toward the side it was last on. Body width 0.12 m gives an off-track limit of about 0.06 m. Mass 0.8 kg and wheel_track 0.12 m give moderate yaw inertia. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend with low rms_error, and possibly some oscillation on the slalom. Next measurements to check: whether base_speed 1.6 finishes under 3 s, whether steering_oscillation is high (which would mean kd or kp is too high), and whether line_loss_events is nonzero on the slalom (which would mean the sensor span or line_loss choice needs changing).
